conviction_note: Q1 OP of 561m already covers 69% of the 810m H1 plan, which leaves Q2 at 249m (5.8% margin against 13.0% in Q1) on flat sales. This company beat its own revised H1 plan by 90% last year and revised its full year at H1 three years running, so a beat plus an FY raise above the IFIS 1,400m recurring bar is the likely addition. Against that: kabutan already flagged further upside, the stock is on 37x plan EPS, it is up 7.5% over 20 days, and last year's big H1 beat drew -3.1% the next day on a cautious FY raise. That puts p_up at 60 on a 6.5% scale (=+1.3). The findings sum to +1.9, the same sign and a similar size.

findings.finding: The revised H1 plan (OP 810m) leaves only 249m for Jun-Aug, against 561m in Q1 (13.0% margin) on near-identical sales (4,290m vs 4,317m). The company's record on its own plans: H1 FY26 actual OP 616m vs revised plan 324m (+90%), and FY26 initial 714m vs actual 1,122m. Q1 orders were +33.8% y/y (4,729m, book-to-bill 1.10) and new gas-turbine capacity is ramping 'stepwise'. Together these make an H1 beat and an FY raise at this print likely; the July FY revision even cut the implied H2 OP (658m to 626m). A raise that takes FY recurring above the IFIS 1,400m is what the release adds.

findings.why_not_priced: The H1 beat is partly priced: anyone can compute the 70.9% progress rate, and kabutan wrote on 07-08 that further upside was expected. What is not priced is the size of the FY raise. The only street number is one IFIS recurring estimate of 1,400m, 6% above plan, while Q1 annualises to about 2,100m of recurring profit. If the market had priced a raise of that size, the stock would sit above its 3,235 post-Q1 close, not at 2,968, roughly 8% below it, on 37x plan EPS.
